clue.text: Leaving with uncle after power cut in shelter

indicators.note: cut means the letter for power is chopped out of the longer word

parts.note: 'uncle' is slang for a pawnbroker, so leaving goods with him is pawning them
P is the standard abbreviation for power in physics

explanation.surface: A relative walks out after a blackout and takes refuge somewhere.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Uncle' is old slang for a pawnbroker. 'Cut' removes P from PAWNING; 'after' and 'in' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: A canvas canopy over a window or doorway gives cover from sun and rain.

clue.text: "About to visit hookers?" provokes scornful response

indicators.note: to visit means the short word for about goes inside the word for prostitutes

parts.note: hookers is slang for prostitutes, whores
CA, short for circa, means about

explanation.surface: Someone asked whether they plan to see prostitutes answers with contempt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About' looks like the start of a question but is the circa abbreviation; 'provokes' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: An exclamation of indifference, dismissing whatever was said as unimportant.

clue.text: One country extremely unfriendly

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I

indicators.note: extremely means take the extreme letters, first and last, of country

explanation.surface: A nation described as thoroughly hostile.
explanation.definitionFit: A cold, frosty manner is an unwelcoming one.

clue.text: Where roasting's likely when Cabinet Minister's touring north

indicators.note: touring means the minister's name travels around the word for when

parts.note: Michael Gove, a long-serving UK Cabinet Minister
as can mean when, as in 'as I left'

explanation.surface: A government minister on a northern tour is likely to be roasted by critics.
explanation.walkthrough: Michael Gove was a British Cabinet Minister (Education Secretary in 2012); 'touring' signals the container.
explanation.definitionFit: A cooker heated by gas is where meat gets roasted.

clue.text: Aussie talks in strange baby language mostly

indicators.note: strange means the letters of baby are rearranged
mostly means the last letter of the language name is dropped

parts.note: Erse is the Gaelic language

explanation.surface: An Australian chats in an odd kind of baby talk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'strange' turns BABY into YABB; 'mostly' trims ERSE to ERS. 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Yabber is Australian slang for chatter, so yabbers means chats or jabbers.

clue.text: Character said: "Why, dream on!" as possibly scornful response

indicators.note: said means the letter is spoken, giving the word it sounds like

parts.note: the character, or letter, U

indicators.note: possibly means the letters of 'Why dream on' plus 'as' may be arranged otherwise

explanation.surface: A figure in a story speaks dismissively, telling someone to keep dreaming.
explanation.walkthrough: The letter U said aloud gives YOU. 'possibly' rearranges WHY DREAM ON AS into ANDWHOSEARMY.
explanation.definitionFit: A defiant retort mocking a threat, implying the speaker has no backing to carry it out.

clue.text: With each attempt to defend government, Liberal gets scornful response

indicators.note: to defend means the attempt surrounds and protects the letter for government

parts.note: a bid is an attempt

explanation.surface: A Liberal sneers at every effort made to shore up the government.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to defend' signals the container; 'With' and 'gets' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: A sarcastic phrase saying something is not important at all.

clue.text: Heavenly goddess? Hardly

parts.note: a deity tied to the ground rather than the sky, so hardly heavenly

explanation.definitionFit: A goddess of the earth, the opposite of a sky deity; also a warm, nurturing woman.

clue.text: You might be lovers

indicators.note: might be means the letters of lovers could become another word

explanation.surface: The reader is told they may be one of a romantic couple.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'You' is the person doing this crossword; 'might be' rearranges LOVERS.
explanation.definitionFit: The person tackling the crossword is someone who works out its clues.

clue.text: May do better featuring backing group

indicators.note: backing means that run is read right to left
featuring means the answer is a run of letters inside these clue words

explanation.surface: May could improve by appearing with a supporting band.
explanation.walkthrough: 'featuring' points into MAY DO BETTER and 'backing' reads YDOB the other way.
explanation.definitionFit: A body is an organised group of people, such as a governing body.

clue.text: Sugar initially boots fat apprentice out — why? Lazy

indicators.note: initially means take the first letter of Sugar
out means the words for fat and apprentice sit outside the boots

parts.note: lard is pig fat
Ugg is a brand of sheepskin boots
L, for learner, stands for an apprentice
Y sounds like why, a standard crossword abbreviation

explanation.surface: Lord Sugar sacks an overweight Apprentice candidate and asks why, calling them idle.
explanation.walkthrough: Alan Sugar hosts the UK TV show The Apprentice, so the surface is a sacking; 'out' signals the outer pieces round the boots.
explanation.definitionFit: A sluggard is an idle person, so sluggardly means slothful.

clue.text: Where you'll save money building 15 — ah, neat!

indicators.note: building means the letters are assembled into a new form

parts.note: 15 in Roman numerals is XV

explanation.surface: An excited remark about a neat money-saving construction project.
explanation.walkthrough: '15' here is the number, not the cross-reference: Roman XV. 'building' rearranges XV, AH and NEAT.
explanation.definitionFit: A country with low tax rates lets people keep more of their wealth.

clue.text: Twice the plate proves problematic for versatile sportsperson

indicators.note: proves problematic means the letters get jumbled into trouble
twice means the word 'the' is written two times

explanation.surface: Getting a double helping on one's plate causes trouble for an all-round athlete.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Twice' gives THETHE; 'proves problematic' rearranges that with PLATE.
explanation.definitionFit: An athlete competing in seven events must be an all-rounder.

clue.text: Earl selected slightly twisted rings

indicators.note: slightly twisted means one letter of the word for selected shifts position a little

parts.note: selected means chose

explanation.surface: A nobleman picks some mildly bent rings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'slightly twisted' moves the S of CHOSE one place along, giving CHOES.
explanation.definitionFit: A bell or sound that rings out resounds, as a voice reverberates in a hall.

clue.text: Taking two spades, broad's going to plant tree

indicators.note: taking means the letters for the spades are taken away

parts.note: broad means sweeping, as in a sweeping statement
will expresses the future, going to
to sow is to plant seed
S is the card abbreviation for spades, so two give SS

explanation.surface: A bridge bid of two spades leads a woman to plant a tree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Taking' removes both S letters from SWEEPING WILL SOW. 'Broad' looks like a woman but means sweeping.
explanation.definitionFit: A willow with long drooping branches is a familiar ornamental species.

clue.text: Over union member Labour come in for praise

indicators.note: over means, in this down light, the rearranged letters sit above the rest
labour means the words come in are worked into another order

explanation.surface: Trade unionists welcome Labour supporters joining them in admiration.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Labour' looks like the party but rearranges COME IN; 'Over' places that above UM in the down entry. 'for' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: An encomium is a formal speech or piece of writing full of high tribute.

clue.text: That hotel keeper's first to react with scornful response

indicators.note: react means the letters respond by rearranging themselves
first means take the opening letter of keeper

parts.note: and can mean with, as in fish and chips

explanation.surface: A hotel manager meets a complaint with contempt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'react' rearranges THAT HOTEL plus K; 'to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A dismissive phrase, said with a raised palm, refusing to listen.

clue.text: Site of 4 on river close to York

indicators.note: on means, in this down light, the letter sits on top of the river
close to means the final letter of York

parts.note: the Itchen is a river in Hampshire

explanation.surface: Somewhere by a river near York houses a cooker.
explanation.walkthrough: 4 is GAS OVEN. 'on' places K above ITCHEN, a river in Hampshire, southern England.
explanation.definitionFit: A cooker is found in the room where meals are prepared.

clue.text: It cuts two ways facing a journalist upfront

indicators.note: upfront means the journalist comes at the front

parts.note: a hack is a journalist

indicators.note: facing means the two compass points face each other with a between them

parts.note: S and W are compass directions, south and west

explanation.surface: Something double-edged confronts a reporter openly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'facing' sets S and W either side of A; 'upfront' puts HACK first.
explanation.definitionFit: A fine-toothed blade in a frame, used to slice through metal.

clue.text: Sore? It hurt, they're right

indicators.note: hurt means the letters are damaged into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone complains of a sore spot that hurt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hurt' rearranges SORE IT.
explanation.definitionFit: Conservatives are on the political right wing.

clue.text: "Rather missing Tyrus" brings scornful response

indicators.note: missing means the setter is left out of the word for rather

parts.note: rather means somewhat
Tyrus is the setter, who refers to themself as me

explanation.surface: The setter's absence draws a contemptuous shrug.
explanation.walkthrough: A setter naming themself means ME. 'missing' removes ME from SOMEWHAT; 'brings' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A dismissive retort meaning the point made doesn't matter.

clue.text: Nice food — there is a load being eaten

indicators.note: being eaten means the load goes inside the French word

parts.note: in Nice, French est means is, so there 'is' gives est
a cargo is a load

explanation.surface: Good food, and plenty of it being consumed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nice' is the French city, not the adjective, which is why the French word for is applies; 'being eaten' signals the container.
explanation.definitionFit: Snails, a French delicacy, eaten in Nice.

clue.text: Murdoch paper runs holiday schemes (might be dodgy)

parts.note: The Times is owned by Rupert Murdoch
hares means runs fast

explanation.surface: A Murdoch newspaper runs a story on shady holiday deals.
explanation.definitionFit: Shared ownership of a holiday property, used by each owner for set weeks; some sales are notoriously shady.

clue.text: Boxer's uppercut finally landed

parts.note: Muhammad Ali, the boxer

indicators.note: finally means take the last letter of uppercut

explanation.surface: A boxer's uppercut at last connects.
explanation.definitionFit: Alit is an old past tense of alight, to come down and settle.

clue.text: Commander of the 17

explanation.definitionFit: An aga is a Turkish military commander; an Aga is a range cooker found in a kitchen.

clue.text: Longing to return to stage here in London

parts.note: a step is a stage

indicators.note: to return means the word for longing comes back reversed

parts.note: a yen is a longing

explanation.surface: Someone yearns to get back on stage in a London district.
explanation.walkthrough: Stepney is a district of east London. 'to return' reads YEN backwards; the second 'to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A district in the East End of London.

clue.text: Big Sam in charge here — gosh, that's a blow!

parts.note: Sam Allardyce, Big Sam, was managing West Ham, written W.HAM
my is an exclamation like gosh

explanation.surface: Big Sam takes charge, prompting an exclamation at a heavy hit.
explanation.walkthrough: Sam Allardyce, a football manager known as Big Sam, managed West Ham United, an east London club, in 2012.
explanation.definitionFit: A whammy is a severe setback or misfortune, as in a double whammy.
